blocks.response_text: The ESO's report says Ipswich Hospital's internal protection operated coincident with the timeframe of the lightning strike, and that UKPN's time-stamped data show the hospital's load reducing by half in a period of 14 seconds [reported].
UKPN confirmed to the ESO that the hospital was not part of its LFDD protection zone and that LFDD did not affect the substations supplying the hospital.

Our trust's public statement of 10 August 2019 [reported], summarised here rather than quoted, described a minor on-site power problem: every standby generator operated, but one breaker serving outpatient services failed to, briefly interrupting electricity to outpatient and x-ray areas; business-continuity plans were invoked, the problem was resolved quickly and other areas were unaffected. The statement gives no times.

The E3C final report says four hospitals were impacted, two disconnected by the LFDD scheme and two by their internal safety systems, all switching automatically to back-up supplies. The E3C interim report describes one hospital, not named, where incorrect protection settings on its own network switched the site to back-up generation and one of its 11 [reported] generators failed to operate.
